note: Independent rejudgment on 2026-11-24 against RFC 4659 Section 3.2.1.1 ("The link-local address shall be included in the Next Hop field if and only if the advertising BGP speaker shares a common subnet with the peer the route is being advertised to [BGP-IPv6]."). Stale cause: applyEgressNextHopScope (forward_next_hop.go) changed in 52e4ae832a, 63afaf0c95, and f2569d1c08 to decode and write through MPNextHopProfile, skip !baseFamily.NeedsNextHop(), guard peer-own next hops, and select the last admitted nonempty AttrModSet; sibling helpers in egress_inject_filter.go also changed while normalizeOrdinaryNextHop kept the same scope delegation. All 7 tagged carriers (TestRFC4659APIVPNv6LinkLocalCommonSubnet, TestRFC4659VPNv6LinkLocalLoopbackGlobal, TestRFC4659StaticVPNv6LinkLocalCommonSubnet, TestRFC4659ForwardVPNv6LinkLocalCommonSubnet, TestRFC4659ForwardVPNv6NextHopRewriteCarriesRD, test/encode/rfc4659-vpnv6-link-local-off-subnet.ci, and interoplab checkVPNFRR) and all 4 producer boundaries were re-read at HEAD. The tagged carriers accurately prove 48-octet zero-RD pair emission on a common subnet (including loopback global under peer-only scope) and 24-octet omission off-subnet (plus third-party omission in checkVPNFRR) WHEN session > link-local is explicitly configured. However, the default-path defect remains unchanged at HEAD: applyLinkLocal is still the sole production assignment of PeerSettings.LinkLocal and accepts an absent leaf, and linkScope.linkLocalNextHop (case nextHopRouterSpeaker) still returns an empty netip.Addr{} whenever configured LinkLocal is unset. On the default configuration path without an explicit link-local leaf, a speaker sharing a common subnet with its peer still omits the required link-local address and emits only 24 octets, and no tagged carrier exercises interface-derived speaker link-local selection. Retain verdict: weak until default-path interface-derived link-local selection is implemented and tested.
